headline: Chips Stumble, Software Soars as Geopolitical Fires Keep Oil Markets on Edge
body_html:
Friday's session closed a turbulent week on a split note, with 298 of 501 tracked names advancing even as the semiconductor complex absorbed a punishing blow. The sector shed 4.34% on the day — the worst reading across all groups — while software climbed 1.91% and homebuilders led every sector with a 2.8% gain, underscoring a pronounced rotation away from chip-heavy positions and toward names with more domestic, rate-sensitive tailwinds. Market breadth held constructive despite the carnage in semis, with advancers outpacing decliners by roughly three to two.

The 'sell chips, buy software' thesis that has surfaced periodically this year reasserted itself with force. MaxLinear cratered 21.54%, Power Integrations dropped 10.46%, and optical-networking name Coherent fell 9.84%, while on the opposite end of the ledger Medpace surged 14.71% and VeriSign added 7.04%. Packaging Corp's 8.76% rise pointed to pockets of resilience in cyclical industrials even as broader materials slipped 0.22%.

Heading into the new week, the geopolitical backdrop remains the dominant macro variable. Physical oil benchmarks are approaching $110 on supply disruptions tied to the Iran conflict, prediction markets suggest Strait of Hormuz traffic may not normalise for a year or more, and a high-stakes diplomatic meeting between Prime Minister Netanyahu and President Trump is scheduled for Tuesday in Washington. Earnings, sanctions headlines, and any signal on Iran talks will set the tone.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Selloff Dominates Friday's Tape
briefs.body: The semiconductor sector was the session's clear laggard, tumbling 4.34% as MaxLinear plunged 21.54% and Power Integrations shed 10.46%. The broad-based weakness reignited debate over stretched chip valuations and renewed the rotation into software, which gained 1.91% on the day and attracted fresh institutional interest.

briefs.headline: Oil Nears $110 as Middle East Supply Risks Intensify
briefs.body: Physical crude benchmarks surged toward $110 per barrel Friday, driven by compounding supply disruptions across the Iran conflict and the ongoing war in Ukraine. Prediction markets now suggest Strait of Hormuz shipping volumes may not return to pre-crisis levels for twelve months or longer, keeping energy traders on high alert heading into the week.

briefs.headline: Netanyahu-Trump Summit Set for Tuesday in Washington
briefs.body: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu is scheduled to meet President Trump at the White House on Tuesday, with Iran's nuclear posture and regional security arrangements expected to dominate the agenda. The meeting arrives as Trump publicly stated that the United States and Iran are engaged in dialogue, though Tehran has signalled it is not yet prepared to finalise an agreement.

briefs.headline: Houthi-Saudi Exchange Escalates Gulf Tension
briefs.body: Saudi air defences intercepted a Houthi attack targeting an oil refinery over the weekend, while an LPG tanker sailing under a Mozambique flag was struck in Iranian waters, according to the Indian embassy. The incidents pushed Yemen closer to full-scale renewed conflict and added a fresh risk premium to energy markets as the new trading week begins.

briefs.headline: Medpace Headlines Healthcare Gainers on Strong Results
briefs.body: Contract research organisation Medpace jumped 14.71% on Friday, the largest single-session advance in the tracked universe, reflecting renewed investor appetite for healthcare services names with visible earnings pipelines. Biosimulation specialist Certara added 5.63%, suggesting the move was not isolated but part of a broader reappraisal of clinical-development sector fundamentals.

briefs.headline: Schlumberger Surges Even as Energy Sector Dips
briefs.body: Oilfield-services giant Schlumberger bucked a 0.54% sector-wide decline to surge 11.01% on Friday, its strongest single-day move in recent memory. Analysts attributed the divergence to company-specific execution and a view that services demand remains structurally supported even if spot crude prices introduce near-term volatility for upstream producers.
